records.claim: Socratic Models (SMs) is a modular framework in which new tasks are formulated as a language-based exchange between pretrained models and other modules, without additional training or finetuning.

records.claim: SMs are quantitatively competitive with zero-shot state-of-the-art on standard benchmarks including image captioning on MS COCO, contextual image captioning on Concadia, and video understanding on MSR-VTT.
records.quote: SMs are quantitatively competitive with zero-shot state-of-the-art on standard benchmarks including (i) image captioning on MS COCO [15, 16], (ii) contextual image captioning and description (improving 11.3 to 38.9 captioning CIDEr on Concadia [17]), and (iii) video understanding with video-to-text retrieval (from 40.7 to 44.7 zero-shot R@1 on MSR-VTT [18]).

records.claim: SMs enable answering free-form questions about first-person videos by assembling video into a language-based world-state history and performing open-ended text-prompted tasks, formulating video understanding as a reading comprehension problem.
records.quote: We show that this is possible with SMs by assembling video into a language-based world-state history (in the form of a short story, or event log), then performing various types of open-ended text-prompted tasks (e.g., answering questions) about that world-state history – i.e., formulating video understanding as a reading comprehension problem, for which modern LMs are proficient.
